sources.title: Criminals Use Generative Artificial Intelligence to Facilitate Financial Fraud (Alert I-120324-PSA)
sources.supports: Criminals clone a relative's voice from short clips; FBI advice to agree a secret word or phrase with family; AI-written messages and fake profiles.

sources.title: North Korea Aggressively Targeting Crypto Industry with Well-Disguised Social Engineering Attacks (Alert I-090324-PSA)
sources.supports: Tailored job offers and 'technical tests' aimed at crypto workers; warning signs include requests to run code or non-standard packages; verify identities through separate channels.

sources.title: Criminals Increasing SIM Swap Schemes to Steal Millions of Dollars from US Public (Alert I-020822-PSA)
sources.supports: 1,611 SIM-swap complaints with more than $68 million in adjusted losses in 2021; methods: social engineering, insider bribery, phishing.

sources.title: North Korea Responsible for $1.5 Billion Bybit Hack (Alert I-022625-PSA)
sources.supports: FBI attribution of the theft of about $1.5 billion from the Bybit exchange on or about 2025-02-21 to North Korean actors ('TraderTraitor').

sources.title: Cyber Criminals Impersonating Brands Using Search Engine Advertisement Services to Defraud Users
sources.supports: Criminals buy search ads that impersonate brands, including crypto exchanges; FBI advice to type the address directly (or use a bookmark) instead of searching.

sources.title: Fictitious Law Firms Targeting Cryptocurrency Scam Victims Offering to Recover Funds
sources.supports: Fake 'recovery' law firms claim to work with the FBI or other agencies and charge victims fees; more than $9.9 million in reported losses from February 2023 to February 2024.

sources.title: Update on criminals impersonating FBI and IC3 staff to re-target fraud victims (Alert I-072026-PSA)
sources.supports: Impersonators use AI-generated video of FBI leaders and spoofed copies of ic3.gov; IC3 has no social media presence and does not recover funds through social platforms.

sources.title: FBI says crypto-related fraud losses hit record $11.4 billion in 2025, with seniors bearing the brunt (report on the IC3 2025 Internet Crime Report)
sources.supports: IC3 2025 figures: about $11.4 billion in crypto-related losses (181,565 complaints); crypto investment fraud $7.2 billion; recovery scams $1.4 billion; AI tracked for the first time (22,364 complaints, $893 million).

sources.title: Protecting Consumers from SIM-Swap and Port-Out Fraud (Report and Order, FCC 23-95)
sources.supports: Rules adopted 2023-11-15 requiring US wireless carriers to use secure authentication before SIM changes and port-outs and to notify customers of such requests (some provisions phased in after OMB review).

sources.title: Implementing Phishing-Resistant MFA (fact sheet)
sources.supports: FIDO/WebAuthn is the only widely available phishing-resistant MFA; SMS and voice codes are exposed to phishing, SS7 and SIM-swap attacks.

sources.title: SP 800-63B-4, Digital Identity Guidelines: Authentication and Authenticator Management
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.supports: Out-of-band authentication over the phone network, including SMS codes, is a 'restricted' authenticator.

sources.title: SECGov X Account (statement on the January 9, 2024 compromise)
sources.supports: The SEC's X account was taken over through a SIM swap of the phone number tied to it; multi-factor authentication had been disabled since mid-2023.

sources.title: Alert on Fraud Schemes Involving Deepfake Media Targeting Financial Institutions (FIN-2024-Alert004)
sources.publisher: Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN), US Treasury
sources.supports: Rising reports since 2023 of generative-AI deepfakes used to defeat identity checks; red flags such as a third-party webcam plugin during live verification.

sources.title: Alert on Prevalent Virtual Currency Investment Scam Commonly Known as 'Pig Butchering' (FIN-2023-Alert005)
sources.publisher: Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN), US Treasury
sources.supports: Relationship investment scams run largely by criminal groups in Southeast Asia, often using trafficked workers; victims are groomed before being shown fake investment platforms.

sources.title: What To Know About Cryptocurrency and Scams
sources.supports: Promises of guaranteed returns are always scams; anyone met on a dating site or app who offers investment advice is a scammer; giveaway scams; report at ReportFraud.ftc.gov.

sources.title: Family Emergency Scams
sources.supports: Some scammers use AI to clone a loved one's voice; call the person back on a number you know is theirs; scammers ask for crypto, wires or gift cards and ask for secrecy.

sources.title: Customer Advisory: AI Won't Turn Trading Bots into Money Machines
sources.supports: Scammers use AI hype to sell trading bots and signal services with promised returns; AI cannot predict the future.

sources.title: Instructions for Form 1099-DA
sources.supports: Brokers report gross proceeds of digital-asset sales made in 2025 without basis; basis reporting applies to covered assets acquired from 2026 and kept in the same account.

sources.title: 2025 Crypto Theft Reaches $3.4 Billion
sources.supports: Over $3.4 billion stolen in 2025 (Bybit $1.5 billion); 158,000 personal-wallet compromises affecting at least 80,000 victims, $713 million stolen from individuals.

sources.title: 2026 Crypto Crime Report: Scams
sources.supports: At least $14 billion received by crypto scams on-chain in 2025 (projected to exceed $17 billion); impersonation scams up 1,400% year on year; AI-enabled scams 4.5 times more profitable.

sources.title: Violent Wrench Attacks Targeting Crypto Holders
sources.supports: Most violent attacks were premeditated, with victims selected through exposed information (data breaches, social media, insiders); publicly disclosing holdings can make people targets.

sources.title: 'Ice phishing' on the blockchain
sources.supports: Attackers trick users into approving the attacker as spender of their tokens; advice to periodically review and revoke token allowances.

sources.title: Think before you Click(Fix): Analyzing the ClickFix social engineering technique
sources.supports: Fake CAPTCHA and error pages trick people into pasting and running malicious commands in the Windows Run dialog, Terminal or PowerShell.

sources.title: Microsoft shares latest intelligence on North Korean and Chinese threat actors at CYBERWARCON
sources.supports: Sapphire Sleet posed as venture capitalists whose online meetings 'failed', then sent a 'fix'; it also posed as recruiters with malicious skills assessments; over $10 million in crypto stolen in six months.

sources.title: Text-to-Malware: How Cybercriminals Weaponize Fake AI-Themed Websites
sources.supports: Fake 'AI video generator' sites promoted through thousands of social media ads that reached millions of users delivered infostealers and backdoors that took logins, cookies and card data.

sources.title: DPRK Adopts EtherHiding: Nation-State Malware Hiding on Blockchains
sources.publisher: Google Cloud Blog (Google Threat Intelligence Group)
sources.supports: Fake recruiters move candidates to Telegram or Discord, then ask for a coding test or project review that downloads malicious code, or show a fake video-call error ('ClickFix') to make them install malware.

sources.title: Bybit Incident Technical Analysis
sources.supports: A rogue interface hid the transaction's intent and sent deceptive data to the hardware wallet; the signer did not verify the details on the device; blind signing and device compromise were the prerequisites.

sources.title: SparkCat trojan stealer infiltrates App Store and Google Play, steals data from photos
sources.supports: Apps in the official App Store and Google Play used on-device OCR to find wallet recovery phrases in photo galleries and upload them.

sources.title: Case study: fake hardware cryptowallet
sources.supports: A counterfeit hardware wallet whose keys were known to the attackers before purchase; the victim lost 1.33 BTC (about $30,000).

sources.title: Copy-paste heist or clipboard-injector attacks on cryptousers
sources.supports: Clipboard-injector malware silently swaps a copied wallet address for the attacker's.

sources.title: Scam Sniffer 2025: Crypto Phishing Losses Fall 83% to $84 Million
sources.supports: Wallet-drainer phishing losses on Ethereum and EVM chains of about $83.85 million in 2025 (106,106 victims), down from about $494 million in 2024; permit and EIP-7702 signature abuse noted; the drainer ecosystem remains active.

sources.title: Blockchain Address Poisoning (USENIX Security 2025)
sources.publisher: Tsuchiya, Dong, Soska and Christin, Carnegie Mellon University
sources.supports: Lookalike addresses that share the first and last characters of a victim's counterparties flood transaction histories; at least $83.8 million lost in 6,633 incidents; about 270 million attempts over two years (CyLab release, 2026-01-07).

sources.title: Exploiter Steals $68M Worth of Crypto Through Address Poisoning
sources.supports: A trader sent 1,155 WBTC (about $68 million) to a poisoned lookalike address; most of it was later returned after negotiation.

sources.title: FoxyWallet: 40+ Malicious Firefox Extensions Exposed
sources.supports: More than 40 fake wallet extensions in Firefox's official add-on store cloned real wallets' open-source code and sent recovery phrases to attackers.

sources.title: Real AI Agents with Fake Memories: Fatal Context Manipulation Attacks on Web3 Agents (arXiv:2503.16248)
sources.publisher: Patlan, Sheng, Hebbar, Mittal and Viswanath (Princeton University, Sentient Foundation)
sources.supports: Injected prompts or poisoned agent memory made AI agents with wallet access perform unauthorized transfers, even where prompt-injection defenses existed.

sources.title: LLM01:2025 Prompt Injection
sources.supports: Instructions hidden in content a model reads (web pages, files) can change its behaviour; fool-proof prevention is unclear; require human approval for high-risk actions.

sources.title: Wintermute warns Pectra upgrade leaves Ethereum users at risk of automated attacks
sources.supports: More than 80% of EIP-7702 delegations pointed to copy-pasted 'sweeper' contracts that drain wallets whose keys have leaked.

sources.title: EIP-2612: Permit Extension for EIP-20 Signed Approvals
sources.supports: A 'permit' changes a token allowance with a signed message instead of a transaction.

sources.title: Ethereum security and scam prevention
sources.supports: The seed phrase is the master key and screenshots may sync to cloud storage; no one from Ethereum will message you or ask for your phrase; airdrop and giveaway scams; never allow remote access; avoid unlimited approvals.

sources.title: How to revoke smart contract allowances/token approvals
sources.supports: Unlimited spending caps let a malicious or hacked app drain a token; revoking is an on-chain transaction that costs gas; disconnecting a site is not the same as revoking.

sources.title: Ongoing phishing campaigns
sources.supports: The wallet maker will never call, DM or ask for the 24-word recovery phrase; there are no circumstances in which you need to give it to anyone.

sources.title: Ledger confirms physical scam letters requesting seed phrase in fake security upgrade
sources.supports: Posted letters using a wallet maker's logo and address asked owners to scan a QR code and enter their recovery phrase for a 'mandatory' check.

sources.title: Set up your 2-step verification
sources.supports: Security keys and passkeys are the strongest options and a second key is recommended as backup; SMS is 'the least secure option'.

sources.title: 'Expect Imposters' Coinbase Tells Customers Whose Information Was Exposed in Data Breach
sources.supports: Criminals bribed overseas support contractors to steal customer data (names, addresses, partial ID numbers, ID images) in order to impersonate the exchange; no passwords, keys or funds were accessed.

sources.title: What is the Global Settings Lock (GSL)?
sources.supports: A settings lock blocks new withdrawal addresses, API key and 2FA changes; unlocking takes a waiting period and triggers an email.

sources.title: How to Enable Withdrawal Whitelist for My Binance Account?
sources.supports: With the whitelist on, withdrawals go only to saved addresses; new addresses can be held for 24, 48 or 72 hours.

sources.title: UK multinational Arup confirmed as victim of HK$200 million deepfake scam
sources.supports: An employee made 15 transfers totalling HK$200 million (about US$25 million) after a video call in which the 'CFO' and colleagues were deepfakes.
